answer: The ocean cap is upheld at intake and ferrous publishes the per-origin counts. At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a walnut tag. A datacenter or proxy pool thus cannot mint a fleet in one epoch whatever the capital it holds, because each account consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. That is 4 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
